claim_boundary.supports: Over an arbitrary type X (Lean, general; the cardinality statement frontier_card is informative only for finite X, frontierEquiv and minimalSelecting_iff_singleton carry the general content): no point is fixed by every permutation when X has two distinct points (the bare-set form of "no Sym(X)-equivariant distinguished-point selection"); a point is invariant under the pointwise stabiliser of a declared set S iff it lies in S or the complement of S is that single point; S selects some point iff S is nonempty or X has exactly one point; for X with two distinct points the inclusion-minimal selecting sets are exactly the singletons, one per point (a consequence of the pointwise-stabiliser definition: a declared point is fixed because it is declared); on a one-point carrier the empty declaration already selects and on an empty carrier nothing does. Replay bound (not part of the Lean claim): exact tables for every subset of every carrier of size 0..6 (127 subsets), invariant points by enumerating all permutations fixing S, and the minimal selecting sets.
claim_boundary.does_not_support: Retention, dynamics or observers being impossible or available (WDP-CH03-N01 is a nonclaim, not formalised); that Selecting / MinimalSelecting formalises WDP-CH03-D01 (D01 minimises declared input sets whose removal restores a symmetry that moves the output, relative to an implementation class and dependency preorder; here the minimal declarations making some point invariant under the pointwise stabiliser are computed, and the two agree on singletons only because the output is the declared point); a Lean notion of equivariant selection function (no_fully_invariant_point is its bare-set specialisation); the price of selection on structured carriers (rigid, cyclic, graph) or under the setwise stabiliser; WDP-CH03-P03; infinite-carrier cardinality; any physical or interpretive claim.
claim_boundary.narrowest_claim: On a bare set of at least two points no point is invariant under all permutations, and in the pointwise-stabiliser model the minimal selecting declarations are exactly the single declared points (price one declared point; price zero on a one-point carrier; no selection on the empty carrier); symmetry-price bookkeeping only.
claim_boundary.next_test: On structured carriers compute the same selecting and minimal tables with Sym(X) replaced by an explicit automorphism group G (n-cycle with rotations, K4 graph with its automorphisms, a rigid carrier with trivial G) and test whether the frontier is still the singletons: a rigid carrier must give price 0 and the n-cycle with rotations price 1; any other value falsifies the claim that the singleton frontier is generic.

report:
# PG-WDP-PROTECTED-QUESTIONS

Mined external Symmetry.lean (FullyInvariantPoint, no_fully_invariant_point: a general swap argument, not vacuous; no selection-function type or equivariance notion exists in it) and the local DAG witness pg_collapse_barrier_protected_questions_and_l1_kkt_trace_embed, which is a fixed instance and partly vacuous (a constant function, the swap on Fin 2, unrelated KKT arithmetic). The ledger D01 definition of the asymmetry-price frontier has no Lean/Rust declaration; it is modelled here by the pointwise stabiliser of a declared set, which is a modelling choice with a different quantifier pattern from D01 (minimal declarations producing invariance versus minimal input sets whose removal frees a symmetry). The node proves the general theorem and the frontier characterisation in Lean and replays exact tables for carriers of size 0..6 with a brute-force permutation checker. The bottleneck WDP-CH03-P03 (declare-then-assert one-item separation) stays unported.

Supported: Over an arbitrary type X (Lean, general; the cardinality statement frontier_card is informative only for finite X, frontierEquiv and minimalSelecting_iff_singleton carry the general content): no point is fixed by every permutation when X has two distinct points (the bare-set form of "no Sym(X)-equivariant distinguished-point selection"); a point is invariant under the pointwise stabiliser of a declared set S iff it lies in S or the complement of S is that single point; S selects some point iff S is nonempty or X has exactly one point; for X with two distinct points the inclusion-minimal selecting sets are exactly the singletons, one per point (a consequence of the pointwise-stabiliser definition: a declared point is fixed because it is declared); on a one-point carrier the empty declaration already selects and on an empty carrier nothing does. Replay bound (not part of the Lean claim): exact tables for every subset of every carrier of size 0..6 (127 subsets), invariant points by enumerating all permutations fixing S, and the minimal selecting sets.

Remaining: Retention, dynamics or observers being impossible or available (WDP-CH03-N01 is a nonclaim, not formalised); that Selecting / MinimalSelecting formalises WDP-CH03-D01 (D01 minimises declared input sets whose removal restores a symmetry that moves the output, relative to an implementation class and dependency preorder; here the minimal declarations making some point invariant under the pointwise stabiliser are computed, and the two agree on singletons only because the output is the declared point); a Lean notion of equivariant selection function (no_fully_invariant_point is its bare-set specialisation); the price of selection on structured carriers (rigid, cyclic, graph) or under the setwise stabiliser; WDP-CH03-P03; infinite-carrier cardinality; any physical or interpretive claim.
